title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (1966 letter to Tate on crystals, §1.12–1.14). k is perfect of characteristic p, W = W(k), K = Frac W, and S is smooth over k. Previously, S was lifted to X proper over W, and the generic fibre X_K was used algebraically. Here only a formal lift X → Spf W is assumed. The previous page states the trivial equivalence {crystals of coherent modules on S/W} ≃ {coherent O_X-modules with stratification relative to Spf W}, where 'stratification' should be read in the PD sense, i.e. an integrable, topologically quasi-nilpotent connection.

(1) Isocrystals. To get the analogue of 'restriction to X_K', Grothendieck says one must take X_K to be the rigid-analytic space over K attached to the formal scheme X. In modern terms this is Raynaud's generic fibre, then 8 years in the future. On X_K one considers coherent modules with rigid-analytic stratification, equivalently integrable connections. These are locally free. Since Γ(X_K, E_K) = Γ(X, E)⊗Q for quasi-compact X, the functor E ↦ E_K kills torsion and induces a fully faithful functor
{isocrystals = coherent crystals with Hom⊗Q} → {coherent O_{X_K}-modules with integrable connection}.
He flags the determination of the essential image as the 'natural' problem, more so than in the algebraic case, where a later marginal note on the previous page says 'ça ne marche pas'. Modern answer: the image lies in the connections whose Taylor series converge on the residue tubes. These are the convergent isocrystals of Ogus (1984) and Berthelot (rigid cohomology), and the convergence condition is the obstruction.

(2) Question. Do coherent stratified modules on a rigid space admit a simple description via a 'more or less discrete' group, playing the role of the topological π1 in the complex theory? This is a p-adic Riemann–Hilbert / fundamental-group question.

(3) Old §1.13 (number deleted). Consequences of the formal description:
- the category of coherent crystals on S is noetherian when S is of finite type;
- every object has a largest torsion sub-object;
- torsion-free crystals correspond to torsion-free stratified O_X-modules, which are claimed to be automatically locally free.
He conjectures analogues without smoothness of S.

(4) §1.14 Functoriality. Given a commutative square S' → S over Spec k' → Spec k, with S' smooth over a perfect k', a formal lift X' and a lift X' → X compatible with Spec W' → Spec W, crystal pullback S → S' becomes ordinary pullback of stratified modules X → X'. This is the set-up for making M ↦ M^(p) explicit through a Frobenius lift. That is done on the next page: the pullback is independent of the lift up to canonical isomorphism, as for Dwork/Berthelot Frobenius structures.
errors: Claim that torsion-free stratified coherent modules on the formal lift X are automatically locally free appears false for PD-stratifications (= crystals). Counterexample: X = Spf W<t>, M = ideal (p, t^p) ⊂ O_X with the connection induced by d. We have ∂(ap + bt^p) = p∂a + t^p∂b + pbt^{p-1} ∈ M, and quasi-nilpotence is inherited from O_X. Intrinsically it is the sub-crystal of O_{S/W} generated by p and any lift of t^p: the choice of lift is irrelevant since (t+x)^p − t^p ∈ pO for x in a PD ideal. M is O-torsion-free and p-torsion-free but not locally free (2 generators, not invertible). The claim holds on X_K, not on X. If 'stratification' is meant in the non-PD infinitesimal sense, this M is not stratified (∂^p/p!(t^p) = 1), but then the 'trivial' equivalence with crystals fails integrally.

'Stratifications au sens rigide-analytique, ou ce qui revient au même, connexions intégrables' hides the key issue. Infinitesimal stratifications on X_K are just integrable connections, while isocrystals give connections satisfying a convergence condition on the tube of the diagonal. So the functor is not essentially surjective. Grothendieck poses this as an open question rather than making a false claim, but the identification glosses over where the answer lies.

ideas.what: Rigid-analytic generic fibre X_K of a formal scheme X over Spf W, used as the home for isocrystals
ideas.modern_name: Raynaud generic fibre / tube; rigid realisation of isocrystals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud (1974) for the generic fibre; Berthelot (late 1970s–1996) for rigid cohomology
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate (1966), known and cited in the crystalline literature; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Fully faithful functor from isocrystals (crystals ⊗Q) to modules with integrable connection on X_K, with the question of its essential image
ideas.modern_name: Convergent isocrystals; convergence (radius) condition characterising the image

ideas.what: Seek a 'more or less discrete' group whose representations describe connections on rigid spaces, as π1 does over C
ideas.modern_name: p-adic Riemann–Hilbert / non-archimedean fundamental groups (de Jong's étale π1 of analytic spaces, André's tempered π1, p-adic Simpson)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Jong (1995), André (2003), Faltings (2005), Scholze, Liu–Zhu (2017)

ideas.what: Crystals = stratified modules on a formal lift; consequences: noetherian category, largest torsion sub-object
ideas.modern_name: Crystals ↔ modules with quasi-nilpotent integrable connection
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Pullback of crystals via lifts of morphisms; Frobenius via a Frobenius lift, independent of choices

missed.claim: As early as 1966, Grothendieck asks for a description of connections on rigid spaces through a 'more or less discrete' group replacing the topological π1. This anticipates André's tempered fundamental group, which is a quasi-discrete prodiscrete group built precisely to handle p-adic connections, and later p-adic Riemann–Hilbert work.
missed.quote: description simple, en termes d'un groupe plus ou moins discret jouant le rôle du groupe fondamental dans la théorie transcendante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically an early formulation of the p-adic Riemann–Hilbert problem. Mathematically, the phrase 'plus ou moins discret' points toward tempered/prodiscrete groups rather than profinite ones, which is still a live design question.

missed.claim: Use of the rigid generic fibre of a formal scheme, and identification of the essential image of isocrystals as the 'natural' open problem, in 1966. This predates Raynaud's generic fibre (1974) and Ogus/Berthelot convergent isocrystals.
missed.quote: il faut définir X_K comme l'espace rigide-analytique sur K défini par le schéma formel X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority/history: the convergent-isocrystal problem was posed by Grothendieck himself. This is likely partially known to specialists via the Tate letter.

deep.surprise_reason: Early (1966) formulation of rigid generic fibres, the convergent-isocrystal problem and a p-adic fundamental-group question, all later solved or developed by others. The letter is known to specialists, so it is notable but not shocking. The page also contains a dubious claim about local freeness of torsion-free crystals.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the handwritten 'envisagée' is inserted above, between X_K and 'plus haut'. Read: 'trouver un analogue pour (struck/overtyped) la restriction à X_K envisagée plus haut'. It does not replace 'pour'.
Deleted paragraph number '1.13.' precedes 'La description donnée'. The insertion is 'des cristaux sur S' and the comma before 'toute triviale' is retained.
'de plus les objets sans torsion correspondent' — 'les' is retyped over and 'ent' is added by hand.
